content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge treats a single verse as UNDERDETERMINED because its wording admits two readings, which is the kind of single-verse openness K-S2 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "“a verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand” — I weighed (1) a verse merely permitting two possible readings, leaving it open, against (2) a verse actually carrying both senses simultaneously, so neither is open and both stand.", "why": "The judge's stated basis is that Matthew 1:16 admits two readings, so it uses single-verse ambiguity as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's bar and its instruction that both senses stand."}
